The only friendly creature on their board is Slickshot Show-Off, which would benefit enormously from the +2/+2 buff (and would also trigger its +2/+0 ability since Mutagenic Growth is a noncreature spell, making it effectively +4/+2). With Slickshot Show-Off being a flying hasty threat, buffing it before combat could deal significant damage or even threaten lethal with additional spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted opponent's Delighted Halfling with Mutagenic Growth
annotations.betterLine: Target Slickshot Show-Off with Mutagenic Growth to maximize combat damage. Slickshot would become a 5/4 flyer (1/2 base + 2/0 from prowess trigger + 2/2 from Mutagenic Growth) heading into combat.

annotations.description: GPT4om Coach is casting Mutagenic Growth (likely paying 2 life, going from 10 to 8) and targeting Dryad Arbor instead of their own Slickshot Show-Off. Mutagenic Growth on Slickshot Show-Off would give it +2/+2 AND trigger its ability for an additional +2/+0, making it a 5/4 flyer. Instead, pumping the opponent's Dryad Arbor accomplishes nothing useful - it makes an opponent's creature bigger. This is either a misclick or a fundamental misunderstanding. The only scenario where this might make sense is if they're trying to save Dryad Arbor from dying to set up some interaction, but there's no reason to help the opponent's creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Dryad Arbor (opponent's creature) with Mutagenic Growth
annotations.betterLine: Target Slickshot Show-Off with Mutagenic Growth to maximize damage output, getting both the +2/+2 from the spell and +2/+0 from Slickshot's trigger for a 5/4 flying attacker

annotations.description: Mutagenic Growth is one of the strongest cards in hand for a Slickshot Show-Off burst kill. It's a free spell (+2/+2 plus Slickshot's +2/+0 trigger = +4 damage for just 2 life). Against Yawgmoth's grinding engine, the Slickshot player needs to assemble a lethal burst turn quickly, and Mutagenic Growth is critical to that plan.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Mutagenic Growth
annotations.betterLine: Discard Arid Mesa (redundant with Wooded Foothills already in hand and two lands in play) or Cori-Steel Cutter (expensive and less synergistic with the burst kill plan). Keeping Mutagenic Growth maximizes the chance of a lethal Slickshot turn with Lava Dart + Mishra's Bauble + Mutagenic Growth.

annotations.description: Spending all 4 available mana on Walking Ballista's {4} ability in precombat main prevents casting Young Wolf or other spells from hand this turn. With Young Wolf in hand costing just {G}, and Yawgmoth on board, casting Young Wolf first would enable the Yawgmoth sacrifice engine and provide more flexibility. The +1/+1 counter on Ballista could potentially wait or the mana could be better used for developing the board.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Walking Ballista's {4} ability to put a +1/+1 counter on it, using all available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Young Wolf for {G} first, potentially cast Badgermole Cub or Agatha's Soul Cauldron with remaining mana, then use Yawgmoth's sacrifice abilities to interact with the opponent's Slickshot Show-Off while drawing cards.

annotations.description: Only attacked with Walking Ballista (likely 1 damage) instead of also attacking with Yawgmoth, Thran Physician (2/4). The opponent's only creature is Slickshot Show-Off (1/2 flying) which can't profitably block Yawgmoth's 2/4 body. Keeping Yawgmoth back provides little defensive value since it can't block the flying Slickshot, and its sacrifice ability requires another creature (none are available untapped). Missing 2 damage when the opponent is at 10 life is meaningful pressure.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Walking Ballista, keeping Yawgmoth back
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Yawgmoth and Walking Ballista to deal 3 damage total instead of 1, pressuring the opponent's 10 life total while Yawgmoth faces no profitable blocks

annotations.description: Lava Dart deals only 1 damage to Yawgmoth, Thran Physician (2/4), which accomplishes nothing - the damage doesn't persist and won't kill it. Even with Lava Dart's flashback (sacrifice Mountain) for a second point, 2 total damage still doesn't kill a 2/4. This completely wastes the Lava Dart's damage output.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Yawgmoth, Thran Physician (2/4) with Lava Dart for 1 damage, dealing inconsequential damage.
annotations.betterLine: Target Dryad Arbor (1/1) to kill it, removing both a mana source and a potential Yawgmoth sacrifice target. Alternatively, target Gem25P Gramps directly to advance the burn/aggro plan with Slickshot Show-Off attacking.

annotations.description: With Lava Dart on the stack (likely targeting Walking Ballista or another creature), Gramps declined to use Walking Ballista's 'remove counter to deal 1 damage' ability or Yawgmoth's sacrifice ability in response. If Ballista is about to die, its +1/+1 counter would be wasted. Yawgmoth could also sacrifice a creature to put a -1/-1 counter on Slickshot Show-Off (which is pumped to 3/2 from prowess) and draw a card.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities in response to Lava Dart on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Use Walking Ballista's remove-counter ability to ping Slickshot Show-Off for 1 before losing the counter, and/or use Yawgmoth to sacrifice Dryad Arbor to put a -1/-1 counter on Show-Off and draw a card, potentially killing it.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Walking Ballista to ping opponent in response to Lava Dart on the stack. If Lava Dart targets the Ballista, failing to remove counters in response wastes damage entirely. Even if not targeting Ballista, with opponent at 9 life against a burn deck, incremental damage matters, especially since Yawgmoth's sacrifice engine in combination with Young Wolf (in hand) can generate value without needing Ballista counters.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Walking Ballista or Yawgmoth
annotations.betterLine: Remove a +1/+1 counter from Walking Ballista to deal 1 damage to the opponent (or to Slickshot Show-Off) in response to Lava Dart, preserving value before potentially losing the Ballista

annotations.description: With Lava Dart on the stack likely targeting Walking Ballista, Gramps declined to activate any abilities in response. Walking Ballista could remove its +1/+1 counter to deal 1 damage before dying, and/or Yawgmoth could sacrifice the Ballista to draw a card and put a -1/-1 counter on Slickshot Show-Off. Passing here wastes significant value from a creature about to die.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Walking Ballista or Yawgmoth, letting Lava Dart resolve and losing the Ballista for nothing.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Walking Ballista to deal 1 damage to Slickshot Show-Off or the opponent, and/or sacrifice it to Yawgmoth to draw a card and potentially shrink/kill the Show-Off. At minimum, ping for 1 damage as pure upside before losing the creature.

annotations.description: Opponent's Lava Dart is on the stack, likely targeting Walking Ballista (which is a 0/0 with +1/+1 counters). Gramps has Yawgmoth, Thran Physician on the battlefield and could sacrifice Walking Ballista to Yawgmoth in response to draw a card and put a -1/-1 counter on Slickshot Show-Off (killing it since it's a 1/2). Instead, Gramps declined to activate any abilities, letting the Lava Dart resolve and losing the Walking Ballista for nothing while leaving the dangerous Slickshot Show-Off alive. Additionally, Walking Ballista itself could remove its counter to deal 1 damage before dying.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities in response to Lava Dart on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Yawgmoth, sacrificing Walking Ballista to put a -1/-1 counter on Slickshot Show-Off and draw a card, or at minimum remove Walking Ballista's +1/+1 counter to ping the opponent or Slickshot Show-Off before the Lava Dart resolves.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 7 life with only a flying Slickshot Show-Off as a blocker. Casting Agatha's Soul Cauldron is a setup card that doesn't contribute to killing the opponent this turn. With Young Wolves and ground attackers (Yawgmoth 2/4, Delighted Halfling 1/2, Dryad Arbor 1/1, Walking Ballista), plus casting both Young Wolves for 2 more power, the ground attack alone likely deals lethal or near-lethal damage. Spending mana on Cauldron instead of deploying creatures for a lethal attack is a significant missed opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Agatha's Soul Cauldron (a setup artifact) before combat
annotations.betterLine: Cast both Young Wolves using land mana, then attack with all ground creatures (Yawgmoth, Walking Ballista, Delighted Halfling, Dryad Arbor, both Young Wolves) for likely lethal damage against 7 life with no ground blockers.

annotations.description: Gem25P Gramps is at 12 life with the opponent at 7 life. Looking at the board, Gramps has Delighted Halfling (1/2), Dryad Arbor (1/1), Yawgmoth (2/4), and Walking Ballista available to attack. The opponent has only Slickshot Show-Off (1/2 flying) as a potential blocker. Attacking with Delighted Halfling (1), Dryad Arbor (1), Yawgmoth (2), and Walking Ballista would deal at least 4 damage (Slickshot can only block one non-flying attacker), bringing opponent to 3 or less. With Yawgmoth's sacrifice ability and Walking Ballista's ping ability, there are likely lethal lines available. Even if not exact lethal this turn, dealing significant damage when the opponent is at 7 life is critical. The player declined to attack at all, confusedly thinking they had already attacked this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures, believing combat had already happened this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all available creatures. Opponent at 7 life can only block one ground creature with Slickshot Show-Off. Attacking with Delighted Halfling, Dryad Arbor, Yawgmoth, and Walking Ballista would push through at least 4-5 damage (likely more), putting the opponent in range of Walking Ballista pings or Yawgmoth sacrifice loops. This could be lethal or near-lethal.

annotations.description: Gem25P Gramps has Yawgmoth, Thran Physician on the battlefield, Walking Ballista (likely with 0 counters but on the field), Young Wolf on the stack about to resolve, and the opponent at 7 life. With Young Wolf resolving, they could sacrifice Young Wolf to Yawgmoth (it comes back with undying and a +1/+1 counter), then sacrifice it again repeatedly if they have enough life or other creatures. More critically, Walking Ballista can be used with Yawgmoth to generate value. But the key missed opportunity is using Walking Ballista's activated ability to ping the opponent - though it may have 0 counters. The real issue is that with Yawgmoth + Young Wolf (undying) + any other creature, Gramps can loop sacrifices to draw cards and put -1/-1 counters on the Slickshot Show-Off or just draw into more resources. The player declined to activate any abilities while Young Wolf was on the stack, passing priority and letting the turn end without exploiting the Yawgmoth engine. With opponent at 7 life and access to Yawgmoth's sacrifice engine plus undying creatures, there was likely a line to deal significant damage or set up a kill.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Walking Ballista, Agatha's Soul Cauldron, or Yawgmoth while Young Wolf was on the stack, passing the turn.
annotations.betterLine: After Young Wolf resolves, use Yawgmoth to sacrifice Young Wolf (pay 1 life, draw a card, put -1/-1 on Slickshot Show-Off). Young Wolf returns with a +1/+1 counter via undying. Then sacrifice Dryad Arbor or other creatures to Yawgmoth to continue drawing cards and putting counters on opponent's creatures. With Agatha's Soul Cauldron available to exile creatures from graveyards and add counters, there may have been a combo loop available to drain the opponent or at minimum kill the Slickshot Show-Off and draw multiple cards.

annotations.description: Casting Dragon's Rage Channeler before playing a land is a sequencing error. GPT4om Coach has multiple land options in hand (Arid Mesa, Wooded Foothills, Steam Vents) and should play a land first to ensure the land drop isn't missed. More importantly, casting DRC before combat means the opponent sees the creature and can plan accordingly, whereas leading with a land drop (especially a fetch land) preserves options. Additionally, if the plan is to attack with Slickshot Show-Off and cast noncreature spells to pump it, casting a creature spell first doesn't trigger Slickshot's ability. The correct sequence would be to play a land first (like Wooded Foothills or Arid Mesa, which can be cracked later for deck thinning and delirium), then consider whether to cast creatures before or after combat based on what spells are available to pump Slickshot.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Dragon's Rage Channeler before playing a land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play a fetch land (Wooded Foothills or Arid Mesa) first, then evaluate whether to cast DRC before or after combat. Playing the land first ensures the land drop isn't forgotten and preserves better sequencing options.

annotations.description: Declined to attack with any creatures when opponent is at 6 life with only two blockers (DRC 3/3 which can't block Yawgmoth due to protection from Humans, and Slickshot Show-Off). Attacking with Yawgmoth, Delighted Halfling, and Dryad Arbor would push through meaningful damage. Even if Slickshot blocks Yawgmoth and DRC blocks one small creature, at least 1-2 damage gets through, putting opponent closer to lethal range for Walking Ballista pings or Yawgmoth drain.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures, passing combat entirely.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Yawgmoth (protected from Human DRC), Delighted Halfling, and Dryad Arbor. Opponent's DRC can't block Yawgmoth, so at minimum Yawgmoth's 2 damage gets through if Slickshot blocks a small creature, or significant total damage if Slickshot blocks Yawgmoth. This pressures the opponent at 6 life and could set up lethal with Yawgmoth sacrifices or Walking Ballista pings.

annotations.description: Gem25P Gramps has Walking Ballista on the battlefield (likely with at least 1 +1/+1 counter), Yawgmoth, Thran Physician, and multiple creatures including Dryad Arbor and Delighted Halfling. The opponent is at 5 life. With Yawgmoth's ability (pay 1 life, sacrifice a creature to draw a card and put a -1/-1 counter on a creature), combined with Walking Ballista's ability to remove counters to deal damage, plus Young Wolf in hand (which has undying for repeated sacrifice loops), there is very likely a line to deal lethal damage this turn. Even without a full combo kill, Walking Ballista can ping the opponent, and Yawgmoth can sacrifice creatures to draw into more resources or directly pressure the opponent's life total. Declining to activate any abilities during combat when the opponent is at 5 life and you have powerful sacrifice/damage outlets available is a critical missed opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities (Walking Ballista, Agatha's Soul Cauldron, or Yawgmoth) during the opponent's combat step, allowing Dragon's Rage Channeler to deal 3 unblocked damage.
annotations.betterLine: Use Walking Ballista to remove counters and ping the opponent for damage. If Walking Ballista has counters, fire them at the opponent's face. Additionally, with Young Wolf in hand (castable next turn) and Yawgmoth on board, the Yawgmoth + Young Wolf + Walking Ballista combo could generate repeated pings. At minimum, any Walking Ballista counters should be used to ping the opponent toward lethal or remove the attacking Dragon's Rage Channeler before damage.

annotations.description: Gem25P Gramps chose no blockers against a 3/3 Dragon's Rage Channeler while at only 9 life, dropping to 6. The reasoning explicitly states they want to block with Yawgmoth (a 2/4 that survives blocking a 3/3), but they failed to actually assign the block. Yawgmoth would have survived the combat and prevented 3 damage, which is critical at such a low life total. The game log shows the Channeler was 'unblocked' despite Yawgmoth being available and the player's own reasoning saying to block with it.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not assign any blockers, letting the 3/3 Dragon's Rage Channeler through unblocked for 3 damage (9 → 6 life).
annotations.betterLine: Block Dragon's Rage Channeler with Yawgmoth, Thran Physician. Yawgmoth (2/4) survives blocking a 3/3, preventing 3 damage and keeping life total at 9 instead of 6. This is especially critical when the opponent has burn potential and Gramps is already at a precarious life total.

annotations.description: When ordering cards for the top of the library from a scry-like effect, putting Cori-Steel Cutter on top would be better than Preordain. GPT4om Coach is at 3 life facing a Yawgmoth combo deck and needs to find action to close the game quickly. Cori-Steel Cutter is an equipment that gives +1/+1, trample, and haste to equipped creatures, and its Flurry ability creates tokens when casting a second spell each turn - this has immediate board impact. Drawing another Preordain just cantrips again, losing a turn of tempo when the player is critically low on life and needs to race. With Slickshot Show-Off, Dragon's Rage Channeler, and Monastery Swiftspear on board, Cori-Steel Cutter would provide meaningful damage increase and trample to push through.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Preordain on top of library (to draw) and Cori-Steel Cutter below it.
annotations.betterLine: Put Cori-Steel Cutter on top to draw it, as it provides immediate board impact with the existing creature-heavy board and the player needs to maximize damage output before Yawgmoth takes over.

annotations.description: Gem25P Gramps declined to use Walking Ballista's activated ability to deal damage to GPT4om Coach, who is at 3 life. Walking Ballista can remove +1/+1 counters to deal 1 damage to any target. If the Ballista has at least 3 counters (or even 1+ counters combined with Yawgmoth sacrifice loops), this could have been lethal. Even with just the Ballista's counters plus Yawgmoth's ability to sacrifice creatures and put -1/-1 counters on opponent's creatures, there were likely lines to deal 3 damage. The opponent then attacked with a 3/3 Dragon's Rage Channeler, dropping Gramps to 3 life — making the game much more precarious. At minimum, Walking Ballista could ping for some damage toward lethal, and Yawgmoth could sacrifice creatures to draw cards and find finishing damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities (Walking Ballista, Agatha's Soul Cauldron, or Yawgmoth) during combat, allowing the opponent's Dragon's Rage Channeler to deal 3 damage unimpeded.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Walking Ballista to remove counters and deal damage to GPT4om Coach (at 3 life). If the Ballista had enough counters, this is lethal. Even if not, combine with Yawgmoth sacrificing Dryad Arbor or Delighted Halfling to draw cards and potentially find additional damage sources, or use the Ballista pings to finish the opponent off.

annotations.description: Discarded Expressive Iteration, one of the most powerful cards in hand for finding burn to close out a game where both players are at 3 life. With Slickshot Show-Off and Monastery Swiftspear on board, Expressive Iteration would also trigger prowess effects.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Expressive Iteration
annotations.betterLine: Discard the second Cori-Steel Cutter or Thundering Falls instead, keeping Expressive Iteration to dig for burn spells or combat tricks to close the game at 3 vs 3 life.

annotations.description: The player spent {4} to put a +1/+1 counter on Walking Ballista instead of simply removing counters to deal damage directly to the opponent. With Walking Ballista having counters (at least 2 based on the reasoning), they could remove counters to deal damage to the opponent at 3 life. Removing 2 counters deals 2 damage, then attacking with remaining creatures could finish the job. But more critically, if Ballista had 2 counters, they should remove them to deal 2 damage, then attack with Yawgmoth (2 power) and/or Dryad Arbor (1 power) and Delighted Halfling (1 power) for lethal. Instead, they spent 4 mana (which they may not even have had optimally available) to add a counter, wasting tempo when they could have been dealing damage immediately. The player's own reasoning says they can remove counters to deal damage, but the action taken was adding a counter instead.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Walking Ballista's {4}: Put a +1/+1 counter on Walking Ballista, spending 4 mana to grow it instead of using its damage ability.
annotations.betterLine: Remove +1/+1 counters from Walking Ballista to deal direct damage to the opponent (at 3 life), then attack with available creatures for lethal. Even removing 2 counters for 2 damage plus attacking with Dryad Arbor or Delighted Halfling would be lethal if the opponent can't block everything.

annotations.description: Walking Ballista has a +1/+1 counter on it. At 3 life each, Gem25P Gramps should be removing the counter to deal 1 damage to GPT4om Coach, then using Yawgmoth to sacrifice a creature (like Dryad Arbor or Delighted Halfling) to put a -1/-1 counter on an opponent's creature and draw a card, potentially finding ways to deal the remaining 2 damage. Instead, they activated the {4}: Put a +1/+1 counter ability, which costs 4 mana and doesn't advance toward killing the opponent. With the opponent at 3 life and having creatures that can attack back for lethal, the priority should be dealing damage NOW. The Ballista can shoot for 1, and Yawgmoth can sacrifice creatures to draw cards looking for more damage or to put -1/-1 counters on blockers. Even better: remove the counter from Walking Ballista to deal 1 damage to the opponent (opponent goes to 2), then sacrifice Walking Ballista to Yawgmoth (draw a card, put -1/-1 on something), and attack with remaining creatures. The opponent only has Monastery Swiftspear and Slickshot Show-Off as untapped potential blockers.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Walking Ballista's {4} ability to add a +1/+1 counter, spending 4 mana without dealing any damage.
annotations.betterLine: Remove the +1/+1 counter from Walking Ballista to deal 1 damage to GPT4om Coach (going to 2 life), then use Yawgmoth to sacrifice Dryad Arbor or Delighted Halfling targeting an opponent's creature for a -1/-1 counter and drawing a card, then attack with remaining creatures to try to push through the final 2 damage.

annotations.description: Missed lethal. Could sacrifice two creatures (Dryad Arbor + Delighted Halfling) to Yawgmoth's ability to put two -1/-1 counters on Slickshot Show-Off (killing it), then attack with Yawgmoth + Badgermole Cub. Monastery Swiftspear is a Human and can't block Yawgmoth (protection from Humans), so Yawgmoth's 2 damage gets through to the opponent at 2 life for lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Yawgmoth's ability during combat, missing the lethal attack line.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Yawgmoth twice (sacrificing Dryad Arbor and Delighted Halfling, paying 2 life) to put two -1/-1 counters on Slickshot Show-Off, killing it. Then attack with Yawgmoth and Badgermole Cub. Swiftspear (Human) can't block Yawgmoth, so at least 2 damage gets through for lethal.

annotations.description: Gem25P Gramps is at 3 life with Yawgmoth, Thran Physician on the battlefield, and the opponent (GPT4om Coach) is at 1 life. Yawgmoth's activated ability costs 1 life and sacrifices a creature to put a -1/-1 counter on a target creature and draw a card. With Badgermole Cub available to sacrifice, Gramps could activate Yawgmoth targeting any of the opponent's creatures (like Monastery Swiftspear or Slickshot Show-Off) to shrink a potential blocker or attacker. More importantly, if Gramps has any way to deal 1 damage to the opponent at 1 life, this is critical. However, the key issue is that Gramps declined to use Agatha's Soul Cauldron or Yawgmoth's ability during combat. Yawgmoth could sacrifice Badgermole Cub to put a -1/-1 counter on a creature like Monastery Swiftspear (making it 0/1) or Slickshot Show-Off, shrinking potential blockers and drawing a card. With the opponent at 1 life, any incremental advantage matters enormously. Declining to use available activated abilities when they could meaningfully impact the board state at this critical life total juncture is a significant error.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Yawgmoth, Thran Physician or Agatha's Soul Cauldron during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Yawgmoth, Thran Physician by sacrificing Badgermole Cub to put a -1/-1 counter on Monastery Swiftspear (shrinking it to 0/1) and drawing a card, potentially finding a way to deal the last point of damage or improving combat math for a lethal attack.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron during combat, which could exile a creature card (like Dragon's Rage Channeler) from the opponent's graveyard and put a +1/+1 counter on an attacking creature. With the opponent at 1 life, making an attacker bigger could be relevant for getting through blockers. The Cauldron activation costs no life and is essentially free upside.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate either Agatha's Soul Cauldron or Yawgmoth, Thran Physician during combat
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Dragon's Rage Channeler in opponent's graveyard, putting a +1/+1 counter on an attacking creature to improve combat math against the 1-life opponent
